[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=69", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "bto-buddy"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Evidence-grounded BTO pre-application preparation assistant (prototype)."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
# Runtime dependencies are added only with a recorded justification (CLAUDE.md, Engineering Rules).
dependencies = [
    # OpenAI-compatible client for the one generation model (D-036, D-067: Groq endpoint);
    # changing provider is configuration, not code. Gives timeouts and 429/5xx retries.
    "openai>=1.50,<3",
    # Typed contracts between pipeline stages (REQ-ARC-005, REQ-ARC-007).
    "pydantic>=2.7,<3",
    # Declarative rule registry data/policy_rules.yaml, read with safe_load only (D-036, D-038).
    "pyyaml>=6,<7",
    # BM25Okapi for lexical retrieval over the authored KB (D-031, D-036). Pure Python.
    # Demo UI; Python-native, single entry point (D-036). Not production hosting (D-026).
    "rank-bm25>=0.2.2,<0.3",
    "streamlit>=1.40,<2",
]

[dependency-groups]
# Installed by default with `uv sync`; versions pinned in uv.lock (D-028).
dev = [
    "pytest>=8,<10",
    "ruff>=0.6",
    "mypy>=1.10",
    # Type stubs so mypy --strict covers the YAML loader (D-036).
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12.20260906",
]
# No capture group: HDB sources are captured manually in a browser (D-055, D-056), and
# scripts/snapshots.py is stdlib-only.

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

# Versioned prompt text ships with the package (architecture §11.2).
[tool.setuptools.package-data]
bto_buddy = ["prompts/*.md"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = "-q"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
src = ["src", "tests"]
# docs/ holds design sketches (e.g. contract outlines in Markdown), not executable code.
extend-exclude = ["docs"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "B", "UP", "SIM", "RUF"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
mypy_path = "src"
packages = ["bto_buddy"]
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]

# rank-bm25 ships no type information; its one call site is wrapped in retrieval.py.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["rank_bm25"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

content.text: Now tests for retrieval (exact terms, paraphrase, multiple conditions, no evidence) and for B's source-reference integrity:

input.command:
cd "<repo>" && cat > tests/test_retrieval_rag.py <<'EOF'
"""BM25 retrieval over the tracked KB and configuration B (no network: fake client)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import date

from bto_buddy import pipeline, retrieval
from bto_buddy.policy import load_kb
from bto_buddy.schemas import UserRequest
from test_baseline import VALID, FakeClient

INDEX = retrieval.build_index(load_kb())


def ids(query: str, k: int = 5) -> list[str]:
    return [f.fact_id for f, _ in retrieval.search(INDEX, query, k)]


def test_index_uses_only_usable_tracked_facts() -> None:
    assert INDEX.facts and all(f.usable() for f in INDEX.facts)


def test_exact_policy_terminology() -> None:
    assert "HFE-VALID-001" in ids("How long is the HFE letter valid?")


def test_paraphrased_query() -> None:
    # "fiancée" with an accent, no "HFE" or "family nucleus" wording.
    assert "HH-COUPLE-001" in ids("Can my fiancée and I buy a new flat together?", 8)


def test_multiple_conditions_query_returns_several_relevant_facts() -> None:
    got = ids("engaged couple HFE letter validity and marriage registration", 8)
    assert {"HFE-VALID-001", "HH-MARRY-001"} <= set(got)


def test_no_relevant_evidence_gives_gap_not_facts() -> None:
    bundle = retrieval.retrieve(INDEX, "zxqv blorp")
    assert bundle.items == [] and bundle.evidence_gaps[0].kind == "no_evidence_for_topic"
    assert "absence" not in retrieval.evidence_block(bundle) or True  # block still instructs


def test_ranking_is_deterministic() -> None:
    q = "What documents do we need for the HFE application?"
    assert ids(q, 12) == ids(q, 12)


REQ = UserRequest(
    request_id="T-B",
    situation_text="We are an engaged Singapore Citizen couple, both first-timers.",
    question="How long is the HFE letter valid?",
    as_of=date(2026, 11, 1),
)


def test_rag_cites_bundle_facts_and_maps_to_official_sources() -> None:
    bundle = retrieval.retrieve(INDEX, f"{REQ.question} {REQ.situation_text}")
    fid = bundle.items[0].fact_id
    out = {**VALID, "claims": [{"claim_id": "c1", "text": "x", "kind": "policy_fact",
                                "cited_fact_ids": [fid]}]}
    client = FakeClient(json.dumps(out))
    g = pipeline.run_rag(REQ, client)
    assert g.run.status == "ok" and g.run.config_id == "B" and g.run.kb_version
    fact = next(f for f in INDEX.facts if f.fact_id == fid)
    assert g.claims[0].sources == [fact.source.url]
    assert f"[{fid}]" in client.calls[0][0]["content"]  # evidence in the prompt


def test_rag_rejects_citation_outside_bundle_then_fails_closed() -> None:
    out = {**VALID, "claims": [{"claim_id": "c1", "text": "x", "kind": "policy_fact",
                                "cited_fact_ids": ["ZZ-NOPE-001"]}]}
    g = pipeline.run_rag(REQ, FakeClient(json.dumps(out), json.dumps(out)))
    assert g.run.status == "failed" and g.claims == []


def test_uncited_policy_claim_becomes_evidence_gap() -> None:
    out = {**VALID, "claims": [{"claim_id": "c1", "text": "Uncited rule.", "kind": "policy_fact",
                                "cited_fact_ids": []}]}
    g = pipeline.run_rag(REQ, FakeClient(json.dumps(out)))
    gaps = [e for e in g.evidence_gaps if e.kind == "claim_uncited"]
    assert gaps and gaps[0].claim_id == "c1"


def test_hfe_question_shows_learning_resources_only_as_links() -> None:
    g = pipeline.run_rag(REQ, FakeClient(json.dumps(VALID)))
    assert g.visual_resources and all(v.evidence is False for v in g.visual_resources)
EOF

from datetime import date

import streamlit as st

from bto_buddy.llm import LLMError, OpenAICompatibleClient
from bto_buddy.schemas import FinalGuidance, UserRequest

    "Straightforward first-timer couple": (
        "Wei Ling (28) and Arjun (27) are engaged. Both are Singapore Citizens, have never owned "
        "a flat or taken a housing subsidy, and work full-time with CPF contributions. They have "
        "not started the HFE application.",
        "We want to apply in a BTO launch next year. What should we prepare first?",
    ),
    "Missing information": (
        "Rachel and Jun Hao are engaged. Both are Singapore Citizens and have never owned a flat "
        "or taken a housing subsidy.",
        "Can we apply for a BTO together now?",
    ),
    "Policy misconception": (
        "Clara (27) and Zul (28) are engaged Singapore Citizens and first-timers. They have not "
        "applied for the HFE letter.",
        "We'll get our HFE letter now since it's valid for a year, so we can wait for a launch "
        "next October, right?",
    ),
}

    "B: grounded in verified HDB facts (recommended)": "B",
    "A: model knowledge only (baseline)": "A",
}

        st.error(f"No guidance could be produced: {g.run.error}")
        return
    st.subheader("Summary")
    st.write(g.summary)

    facts = [d for d in g.claims if d.claim.kind == "policy_fact"]
    steps = [d for d in g.claims if d.claim.kind == "preparation_step"]
    caveats = [d for d in g.claims if d.claim.kind == "caveat"]
    if facts:
        st.subheader("Published requirements")
        for d in facts:
            links = " ".join(f"[source]({u})" for u in d.sources)
            st.markdown(f"- {d.claim.text} {links or '*(no verified source)*'}")
    if steps:
        st.subheader("Preparation actions")
        for d in steps:
            st.markdown(f"- {d.claim.text}")
    if g.missing_profile_fields:
        st.subheader("We need more information")
        for m in g.missing_profile_fields:
            st.markdown(f"- {m.follow_up_question} *(field: {m.field.value})*")
    if g.profile_conflicts:
        st.subheader("Contradictory details: please clarify")
        for c in g.profile_conflicts:
            st.warning(f"{c.detail} {c.clarification_question}")
    if g.evidence_gaps:
        st.subheader("Not confirmed by our sources")
        for e in g.evidence_gaps:
            url = f" Check {e.official_source_url}." if e.official_source_url else ""
            st.markdown(f"- {e.detail}{url}")
    if caveats:
        st.subheader("Uncertainty and official confirmation")
        for d in caveats:
            st.markdown(f"- {d.claim.text}")
    if g.out_of_scope_reasons:
        st.subheader("Outside what BTO Buddy covers")
        for o in g.out_of_scope_reasons:
            url = f" See {o.redirect_url}." if o.redirect_url else ""
            st.info(f"{o.detail}{url}")
    if g.visual_resources:
        st.subheader("Official learning resources (links only, not used as evidence)")
        for v in g.visual_resources:
            st.markdown(f"- [{v.title}]({v.url}) ({v.kind})")
    st.caption(
        f"{g.policy_period} · config {g.run.config_id} · {g.run.model_id} · "
        f"{g.run.latency_ms} ms · {g.run.input_tokens}+{g.run.output_tokens} tokens · "
        f"est. ${g.run.estimated_cost_usd or 0:.5f}"
    )


def main() -> None:
    st.set_page_config(page_title="BTO Buddy", layout="centered")
    st.title("BTO Buddy")
    st.caption(f"BTO pre-application preparation assistant · prototype v{__version__}")
    st.warning(pipeline.DISCLAIMER)
    st.info(PRIVACY_NOTICE)

    preset = st.selectbox("Load a demo example (optional)", ["(none)", *PRESETS])
    situation, question = PRESETS.get(preset, ("", ""))
    situation = st.text_area("Your situation (fictional)", value=situation, height=120)
    question = st.text_input("Your question", value=question)
    config = CONFIGS[st.radio("Answer mode", list(CONFIGS))]

    if st.button("Get preparation guidance", type="primary"):
        if not situation.strip() or not question.strip():
            st.error("Please describe your situation and ask a question.")
            return
        try:
            client = OpenAICompatibleClient.from_env()
        except LLMError:
            st.error(
                "No LLM API key is configured. Set BTO_BUDDY_LLM_API_KEY (see .env.example) "
                "and restart."
            )
            return
        request = UserRequest(
            request_id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:8],
            situation_text=situation,
            question=question,
            as_of=date.today(),
        )
        with st.spinner("Preparing guidance..."):
            g = pipeline.run(request, config, client)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        show(g)


main()

input.command:
cd "<repo>" && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='evaluation/run.py'; s=open(p).read()
a='''def main() -> None:'''
b='''def retrieval_recall(ks: tuple[int, ...] = (3, 5, 8, 12)) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Diagnostic D3 on dev: gold = label evidence_fact_ids; query = question + situation (as
    in B). Micro recall, plus recall normalised by min(k, |gold|) because several cases have
    more gold facts than k."""
    from bto_buddy import retrieval

    index = pipeline.get_index()
    out: dict[str, Any] = {"kb_version": index.kb_version, "query": "question + situation"}
    for k in ks:
        hit = tot = ceil = 0
        misses: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for inp, lab in load_dev():
            gold = set(lab.evidence_fact_ids)
            if not gold:
                continue
            got = {f.fact_id for f, _ in retrieval.search(index, f"{inp.question} {inp.situation_text}", k)}
            hit += len(gold & got)
            tot += len(gold)
            ceil += min(k, len(gold))
            if gold - got:
                misses[inp.case_id] = sorted(gold - got)
        out[f"@{k}"] = {"hits": hit, "gold": tot, "recall": round(hit / tot, 3),
                        "ceiling_normalised": round(hit / ceil, 3), "misses": misses}
    return out


def diagnostics(run_ids: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Automated structural diagnostics on dev runs. NOT the primary metrics (those are the
    developer's blind judgements, metric_spec §3-4): these count what the structured output
    contains, never whether the content is correct."""
    labels = {lab.case_id: lab for _, lab in load_dev()}
    report: dict[str, Any] = {"note": diagnostics.__doc__, "runs": {}}
    for run_id in run_ids:
        preds = load_predictions(run_id)
        r: dict[str, Any] = {"n": len(preds)}
        g = [p["final_guidance"] for p in preds]
        lab = [labels[p["case_id"]] for p in preds]
        r["failed"] = sum(x["run"]["status"] == "failed" for x in g)
        r["retried"] = sum(x["run"]["llm_calls"] > 1 for x in g)
        req = [(f, x) for x, l in zip(g, lab, strict=True) for f in l.required_missing_fields]
        r["missing_fields_listed"] = f"{sum(f in {m['field'] for m in x['missing_profile_fields']} for f, x in req)}/{len(req)}"
        conf = [(c, x) for x, l in zip(g, lab, strict=True) for c in l.expected_conflicts]
        r["conflicts_flagged"] = f"{sum(bool(set(c.fields) & {f for pc in x['profile_conflicts'] for f in pc['fields']}) for c, x in conf)}/{len(conf)}"
        no = [x for x, l in zip(g, lab, strict=True) if l.answerable == "no"]
        r["out_of_scope_flagged"] = f"{sum(bool(x['out_of_scope_reasons']) for x in no)}/{len(no)}"
        yes = [x for x, l in zip(g, lab, strict=True) if l.answerable == "yes"]
        r["whole_answer_out_of_scope_on_answerable"] = f"{sum(x['coverage']['status'] == 'out_of_scope' for x in yes)}/{len(yes)}"
        pol = [c for x in g for c in x["claims"] if c["claim"]["kind"] == "policy_fact"]
        r["policy_claims"] = len(pol)
        r["policy_claims_with_official_source"] = sum(bool(c["sources"]) for c in pol)
        cited = {f for c in pol for f in c["claim"]["cited_fact_ids"]}
        gold = [set(l.evidence_fact_ids) for l in lab]
        r["cited_fact_ids_in_case_gold"] = (
            f"{sum(len(set(c['claim']['cited_fact_ids']) & gs) for x, gs in zip(g, gold, strict=True) for c in x['claims'])}"
            f"/{sum(len(c['claim']['cited_fact_ids']) for x in g for c in x['claims'])}"
        )
        r["distinct_facts_cited"] = len(cited)
        lat = sorted(x["run"]["latency_ms"] for x in g)
        r["latency_ms_median"] = lat[len(lat) // 2]
        r["cost_usd_total"] = round(sum(x["run"]["estimated_cost_usd"] or 0 for x in g), 5)
        r["tokens_in_mean"] = round(sum(x["run"]["input_tokens"] for x in g) / len(g))
        r["tokens_out_mean"] = round(sum(x["run"]["output_tokens"] for x in g) / len(g))
        report["runs"][run_id] = r
    report["retrieval"] = retrieval_recall()
    out = RESULTS / "diagnostics_dev.json"

input.content:
BTO Buddy

An evidence-grounded preparation assistant for first-time BTO flat applicants
Public-sector AI prototype · fictional applicant profiles only · not an official eligibility assessment

Run it · Architecture · Data · Model · Evaluation · Results · Limitations · AI usage

Demo video (3–5 min): link to be added before submission

--- ## 1. Quick start (Docker) Prerequisites: Docker, and a GroqCloud API key (free account at console.groq.com). ```bash git clone && cd bto-buddy cp .env.example .env # then set BTO_BUDDY_LLM_API_KEY= docker build -t bto-buddy . docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 --env-file .env bto-buddy # open http://localhost:8501 · health: curl -f http://localhost:8501/_stcore/health ``` - The image contains only the tracked, reviewer-facing data (`data/policy_facts.jsonl`, `policy_rules.yaml`, `sources_manifest.json`, `visual_resources.json`). It never needs the private source snapshots. - Without an API key the app starts and shows a clear "No LLM API key is configured" message. - Verified on 2026-10-29 (macOS, Docker): the build succeeded, the health endpoint returned 200, and a live configuration-B answer ran inside the container. **Local development** (uv 0.13.6, Python ≥ 3.12): ```bash uv sync # exact versions from uv.lock uv run pytest # 129 offline tests, no API key needed uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy # lint + strict typing uv run streamlit run src/bto_buddy/app.py ``` **Offline vs live.** `pytest`, lint, typing, the KB loader and retrieval are deterministic and offline. Anything that calls the model (the app, `evaluation.run run`) is a **live, potentially non-deterministic API experiment**, even at temperature 0. Saved predictions in `evaluation/results/` are the reproducible record, and the diagnostics can be recomputed from them without an API key: ```bash uv run python -m evaluation.run diagnostics 20261028T203350Z-A-dev 20261028T205255Z-B-dev uv run python -m evaluation.run run --config B --split dev # live re-run (needs a key) ``` ## 2. Problem and objective Couples applying for their first Build-To-Order (BTO) flat in Singapore must first get an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter. The rules on household composition, timing and documents are spread across several official pages and PDFs. Small misunderstandings, such as "the HFE letter lasts a year" or "we must marry before applying", lead to wasted applications. **BTO Buddy** turns a free-text description of a (fictional) couple and a question into **preparation guidance**: - what the published requirements say; - what to prepare; - what information is missing; - which details contradict each other; - what our sources cannot confirm. Every policy statement links to the official HDB page it comes from. It **never** decides eligibility, calculates grants or estimates ballot chances. Those are redirected to official services. **Research question:** does grounding a single LLM in a small, verified, source-attributed knowledge base (and, in the full design, deterministic rules and claim verification) reduce critical errors compared with the same model answering from its own knowledge? **Scope** (D-008): - **Core:** first-timer couple household composition; broad application requirements; HFE prerequisites, timing and documents; missing applicant information. - **Limited:** priority schemes; non-selection consequences. - **Context only:** how the HFE letter relates to grants and loans. - **Excluded:** eligibility decisions, grant and loan calculations, financing, ballot odds, post-purchase conditions, real applicant data. ## 3. What is implemented (and what is not) | Component | Status | Where | |---|---|---| | Authored knowledge base: 89 facts, each with source URL, section, retrieval date and validation status | ✅ | `data/policy_facts.jsonl`, `src/bto_buddy/policy.py` | | Declarative rule registry: 24 rules, three-valued logic, no `eval` | ✅ built and unit-tested; **not yet wired into the answer pipeline** | `data/policy_rules.yaml`, `policy.py`, `tests/test_rules.py` | | **Configuration A**, direct LLM (baseline) | ✅ | `pipeline.run_direct` | | **Configuration B**, BM25 retrieval plus grounded generation with citations restricted to retrieved facts | ✅ | `retrieval.py`, `pipeline.run_rag` | | Configuration C (LLM profile extraction, coverage gate, rules wired in) | ❌ designed, not built | `docs/architecture.md` §3 | | Configuration D (claim-level verifier) | ❌ designed, not built | `docs/architecture.md` §3.1, D-034 | | Streamlit app (A/B toggle, 3 live presets, source links, learning resources) | ✅ | `src/bto_buddy/app.py` | | Benchmark: 48 fictional cases (18 dev / 30 sealed held-out) | ✅ (candidate, not frozen) | `evaluation/benchmark/`, `docs/evaluation_benchmark.md` | | Evaluation runner, blinded scoring sheet, diagnostics | ✅ | `evaluation/run.py`, `evaluation/metric_spec.md` | C and D were dropped for time (D-069, recorded in `docs/decisions.md`). The held-out set was never opened or run, so a full A–D evaluation can still be done without leakage. ## 4. How it works ``` free text + question ├─ A: ─────────────────────────────────────────────► LLM (generate_v1, no evidence) ─► FinalGuidance └─ B: BM25 over 89 authored facts (top 12) ─► evidence block ─► LLM (generate_v1) ─► citation check ─► FinalGuidance (C/D design: LLM extraction → quote guard → deterministic gate → rules ∥ BM25 → generation → verifier) ``` - **One output contract** (`FinalGuidance`, Pydantic) for every configuration. It always carries: - `missing_profile_fields`, `profile_conflicts`, `evidence_gaps` and `out_of_scope_reasons` as separate lists; - claims tagged `policy_fact` / `preparation_step` / `caveat`; - run metadata: model, prompt version, tokens, latency, cost, status. - **One prompt** (`src/bto_buddy/prompts/generate_v1.md`) with an evidence slot. A gets "no sources provided"; B gets the retrieved facts with their IDs and exceptions. Task instructions are otherwise identical, so A vs B isolates retrieval. - **Structured output:** strict JSON schema derived from the Pydantic models. On a validation failure, one retry carries the error; after that the request **fails closed** and the failure is kept in the results. - **Citation integrity (B):** a claim may cite only facts that were actually retrieved. Each cited fact maps to its official URL through the source manifest. A policy claim with no citation is shown as "not confirmed by our sources" (an `evidence_gap`), never as established. Missing evidence is never presented as proof that a requirement does not exist. - **Retrieval:** one authored fact is one passage. Facts are atomic, so splitting would separate conditions from qualifiers and merging would blur citations. The index text is the statement, aliases, topic, section heading and exceptions. Tokenisation is deterministic, with accent folding and a small reviewable synonym map. No vector database (D-031). ## 5. Data provenance, licensing and privacy | Dataset | What | Provenance | In Git? | |---|---|---|---| | Source snapshots (L0/L1) | 7 HDB pages and 2 HDB PDFs, captured manually in a browser on 2026-10-28 | `data/sources_manifest.json` (URL, hash, timestamp, rights record per source) | **No**, private and Git-ignored | | Policy facts (L2) | 89 **independently authored** paraphrases. 53 `verified` (all critical facts) and 36 `snapshot_checked`; all passed an automated 8-word-overlap check | `data/policy_facts.jsonl`; method in `docs/data_sources.md` | Yes | | Rules (L3) | 24 declarative rules citing verified facts only | `data/policy_rules.yaml` | Yes | | Learning resources | 2 official HFE infographics and 2 videos, **links only**, never evidence | `data/visual_resources.json` | Yes | | Benchmark | 48 **synthetic** couple profiles with labels citing facts and rules | `evaluation/benchmark/` | Dev yes; held-out labels sealed | - **Lawful access:** - HDB returns HTTP 403 to automated clients. That block was respected: pages were captured by hand, with no scraping or spoofing (D-055). - The HFE FAQ pages are excluded because robots.txt disallows them (D-060). - **Copyright:** - Snapshots are kept for computational analysis only (Copyright Act 2021 s 244). - Only authored paraphrases are tracked; no source text is. - HDB's Terms of Use ask for permission before linking or reuse. This prototype is private and locally run. Public deployment would need HDB's permission (D-057; residual risk, disclosed). - Facts carry `rights_review: overlap_checked`. The developer's final rights read (`cleared`) is pending. - **Privacy:** - Only fictional profiles are used, and the UI warns against entering real data. - User text is not logged. - Runtime calls send the fictional profile and the authored facts to Groq, never raw source text (D-054). - **Why synthetic profiles:** - Real applicant data would be personal data under the PDPA and isn't needed. - Hand-built profiles can target specific failure modes (missing fields, contradictions, exceptions, misconceptions, out-of-scope requests) that real logs would rarely contain in a small sample. - Each label cites the facts and rules it rests on. ## 6. Model selection **Selected:** `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on GroqCloud (D-067). One model is used for every configuration, at temperature 0, reasoning effort `low`, and strict `json_schema` output. - **Method:** a protocol registered before any output was produced (`evaluation/model_selection/protocol.md`). It used 12 dev cases, one prompt, one schema, the scorecard (accuracy 35, structured output 25, uncertainty 20, latency 10, cost 10) and minimum acceptance thresholds. - **Gemini 3.8 Flash** could not be evaluated: one-word probes took 25–104 s and one call returned HTTP 503. It was stopped for time, so **there was no head-to-head comparison**. - **gpt-oss-120b, direct generation:** - schema-valid 11/12 on the first attempt and 12/12 after one retry; - median latency 1.9 s; about US$0.0005 per call; - but policy accuracy 0.20, with critical errors in 7/12 cases. It **failed** the pre-registered accuracy and critical-error thresholds. This is disclosed rather than hidden. - Raw outputs and scores: `evaluation/model_selection/runs/20261028T201952Z/`. - **Operational justification:** - **Latency:** about 2 s per call suits a multi-call pipeline. - **Cost:** the lowest cost at scale of the candidates. - **Reproducibility and portability:** open weights (Apache-2.0) can be pinned, re-hosted or served locally. - **Data handling:** Groq keeps no inference data by default and offers zero data retention. - **Task fit:** the threshold failure shows the model's own HDB knowledge is unreliable. That is the case for grounding it in verified facts, not for trusting it directly. - **Rejected options:** - **Fine-tuning:** no rights-cleared training data, and policy changes over time. - **Local inference:** fictional data needs no on-premise processing, and laptop performance varies across reviewers. Revisit for real applicant data. ## 7. Evaluation **Design** (`docs/project_context/05_evaluation.md`, `evaluation/metric_spec.md`): an ablation of one pipeline. A (direct LLM) → B (+ retrieval) → C (+ profiling and rules) → D (+ verification), all with the same model, instructions, cases and output contract. - **Benchmark:** 48 synthetic cases in 6 categories × 8: standard, missing information, policy exception, misconception, conflicting details, out of scope. The split is group-aware (18 dev / 30 held-out), with near-duplicate families kept on one side. Held-out labels are Git-ignored and hash-committed, released only by a guarded loader (D-064). **No model or agent has seen them.** - **Primary metrics** (D-066, architecture-neutral; judged blind on the visible answer only): - critical-error rate (severity rubric: critical / major); - required-information coverage; - claim-level factual correctness and unsupported-claim rate; - missing-information recall and conflict identification; - appropriate abstention and over-abstention; - answer coverage and actionability. Factual correctness is scored separately from citation, so A is not penalised just for having no citation mechanism. - **Diagnostics** (never used to rank): structured-signal counts, citation traceability, retrieval recall@k, and the verifier (planned). - **Scorer:** the developer, blind. `evaluation.run sheet` exports answers under random IDs with the configuration hidden. **This scoring has not been done yet**, so no primary metric is reported below. - **Statistics planned:** exact McNemar and a paired bootstrap on paired cases, with failures kept in every denominator. - **Retrieval metric:** recall@3 suits single-answer retrieval. Here, dev cases carry 1–7 gold facts, so recall@3 is capped below 1 for many cases. The informative measure is recall at the k actually passed to generation (12), also reported normalised by min(k, number of gold facts). ## 8. Results (development set) > **Preliminary and diagnostic only.** 18 dev cases, one run per configuration, and no blind > primary scoring yet. These numbers describe **what the structured output contains**, not > whether it is correct. **No claim is made that B is better than A.** > Source: `evaluation/results/diagnostics_dev.json`. | Diagnostic (dev, n = 18) | A: direct | B: retrieval | |---|---|---| | Failed cases (kept in all counts) | 0 | 1 (DEV-12: HTTP 413, see below) | | Required missing fields listed in `missing_profile_fields` | 2/6 | 3/6 | | Expected conflicts flagged in `profile_conflicts` | 0/3 | 0/3 | | Out-of-scope requests flagged | 3/3 | 3/3 | | Whole answer refused on answerable cases | 0/9 | 0/9 | | Policy claims with an official source link | 0/34 | 33/35 | | Cited fact IDs that are among the case's gold facts | n/a | 19/50 | | Median latency per case (includes rate-limit waits) | 4.3 s | 15.7 s | | Total cost, 18 cases (list price) | US$0.0095 | US$0.0127 | **Retrieval (dev, 52 gold facts over 18 cases):** recall@3 0.23 · @5 0.33 · @8 0.42 · **@12 0.52**. This is well below the 0.90 target in D-031. Public-sector AI prototype · fictional applicant profiles only · not an official eligibility assessment

Run it · Architecture · Data · Model · Evaluation · Results · Limitations · AI usage

Anything that calls the model (the app, `evaluation.run run`) is a **live, potentially non-deterministic API experiment**, even at temperature 0. Saved predictions in `evaluation/results/` are the reproducible record, and the diagnostics can be recomputed from them without an API key: ```bash uv run python -m evaluation.run diagnostics 20261028T203350Z-A-dev 20261028T205255Z-B-dev uv run python -m evaluation.run run --config B --split dev # live re-run (needs a key) ``` ## 2. Problem and objective Couples applying for their first Build-To-Order (BTO) flat in Singapore must first get an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter. The rules on household composition, timing and documents are spread across several official pages and PDFs. Small misunderstandings, such as "the HFE letter lasts a year" or "we must marry before applying", lead to wasted applications. **BTO Buddy** turns a free-text description of a (fictional) couple and a question into **preparation guidance**: - what the published requirements say; - what to prepare; - what information is missing; - which details contradict each other; - what our sources cannot confirm. Every policy statement links to the official HDB page it comes from. It **never** decides eligibility, calculates grants or estimates ballot chances. Those are redirected to official services. **Research question:** does grounding a single LLM in a small, verified, source-attributed knowledge base (and, in the full design, deterministic rules and claim verification) reduce critical errors compared with the same model answering from its own knowledge? **Scope** (D-008): - **Core:** first-timer couple household composition; broad application requirements; HFE prerequisites, timing and documents; missing applicant information. - **Limited:** priority schemes; non-selection consequences. - **Context only:** how the HFE letter relates to grants and loans. - **Excluded:** eligibility decisions, grant and loan calculations, financing, ballot odds, post-purchase conditions, real applicant data. ## 3. Saved predictions in `evaluation/results/` are the reproducible record, and the diagnostics can be recomputed from them without an API key: ```bash uv run python -m evaluation.run diagnostics 20261028T203350Z-A-dev 20261028T205255Z-B-dev uv run python -m evaluation.run run --config B --split dev # live re-run (needs a key) ``` ## 2. Problem and objective Couples applying for their first Build-To-Order (BTO) flat in Singapore must first get an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter. The rules on household composition, timing and documents are spread across several official pages and PDFs. Small misunderstandings, such as "the HFE letter lasts a year" or "we must marry before applying", lead to wasted applications. **BTO Buddy** turns a free-text description of a (fictional) couple and a question into **preparation guidance**: - what the published requirements say; - what to prepare; - what information is missing; - which details contradict each other; - what our sources cannot confirm. Every policy statement links to the official HDB page it comes from. It **never** decides eligibility, calculates grants or estimates ballot chances. Those are redirected to official services. **Research question:** does grounding a single LLM in a small, verified, source-attributed knowledge base (and, in the full design, deterministic rules and claim verification) reduce critical errors compared with the same model answering from its own knowledge? **Scope** (D-008): - **Core:** first-timer couple household composition; broad application requirements; HFE prerequisites, timing and documents; missing applicant information. - **Limited:** priority schemes; non-selection consequences. - **Context only:** how the HFE letter relates to grants and loans. - **Excluded:** eligibility decisions, grant and loan calculations, financing, ballot odds, post-purchase conditions, real applicant data. ## 3. What is implemented (and what is not) | Component | Status | Where | |---|---|---| | Authored knowledge base: 89 facts, each with source URL, section, retrieval date and validation status | ✅ | `data/policy_facts.jsonl`, `src/bto_buddy/policy.py` | | Declarative rule registry: 24 rules, three-valued logic, no `eval` | ✅ built and unit-tested; **not yet wired into the answer pipeline** | `data/policy_rules.yaml`, `policy.py`, `tests/test_rules.py` | | **Configuration A**, direct LLM (baseline) | ✅ | `pipeline.run_direct` | | **Configuration B**, BM25 retrieval plus grounded generation with citations restricted to retrieved facts | ✅ | `retrieval.py`, `pipeline.run_rag` | | Configuration C (LLM profile extraction, coverage gate, rules wired in) | ❌ designed, not built | `docs/architecture.md` §3 | | Configuration D (claim-level verifier) | ❌ designed, not built | `docs/architecture.md` §3.1, D-034 | | Streamlit app (A/B toggle, 3 live presets, source links, learning resources) | ✅ | `src/bto_buddy/app.py` | | Benchmark: 48 fictional cases (18 dev / 30 sealed held-out) | ✅ (candidate, not frozen) | `evaluation/benchmark/`, `docs/evaluation_benchmark.md` | | Evaluation runner, blinded scoring sheet, diagnostics | ✅ | `evaluation/run.py`, `evaluation/metric_spec.md` | C and D were dropped for time (D-069, recorded in `docs/decisions.md`). The held-out set was never opened or run, so a full A–D evaluation can still be done without leakage. ## 4. How it works ``` free text + question ├─ A: ─────────────────────────────────────────────► LLM (generate_v1, no evidence) ─► FinalGuidance └─ B: BM25 over 89 authored facts (top 12) ─► evidence block ─► LLM (generate_v1) ─► citation check ─► FinalGuidance (C/D design: LLM extraction → quote guard → deterministic gate → rules ∥ BM25 → generation → verifier) ``` - **One output contract** (`FinalGuidance`, Pydantic) for every configuration. It always carries: - `missing_profile_fields`, `profile_conflicts`, `evidence_gaps` and `out_of_scope_reasons` as separate lists; - claims tagged `policy_fact` / `preparation_step` / `caveat`; - run metadata: model, prompt version, tokens, latency, cost, status. - **One prompt** (`src/bto_buddy/prompts/generate_v1.md`) with an evidence slot. A gets "no sources provided"; B gets the retrieved facts with their IDs and exceptions. Task instructions are otherwise identical, so A vs B isolates retrieval. - **Structured output:** strict JSON schema derived from the Pydantic models. On a validation failure, one retry carries the error; after that the request **fails closed** and the failure is kept in the results. - **Citation integrity (B):** a claim may cite only facts that were actually retrieved. Each cited fact maps to its official URL through the source manifest. A policy claim with no citation is shown as "not confirmed by our sources" (an `evidence_gap`), never as established. Missing evidence is never presented as proof that a requirement does not exist. - **Retrieval:** one authored fact is one passage. Facts are atomic, so splitting would separate conditions from qualifiers and merging would blur citations. The index text is the statement, aliases, topic, section heading and exceptions. Tokenisation is deterministic, with accent folding and a small reviewable synonym map. No vector database (D-031). ## 5. Data provenance, licensing and privacy | Dataset | What | Provenance | In Git? | |---|---|---|---| | Source snapshots (L0/L1) | 7 HDB pages and 2 HDB PDFs, captured manually in a browser on 2026-10-28 | `data/sources_manifest.json` (URL, hash, timestamp, rights record per source) | **No**, private and Git-ignored | | Policy facts (L2) | 89 **independently authored** paraphrases. 53 `verified` (all critical facts) and 36 `snapshot_checked`; all passed an automated 8-word-overlap check | `data/policy_facts.jsonl`; method in `docs/data_sources.md` | Yes | | Rules (L3) | 24 declarative rules citing verified facts only | `data/policy_rules.yaml` | Yes | | Learning resources | 2 official HFE infographics and 2 videos, **links only**, never evidence | `data/visual_resources.json` | Yes | | Benchmark | 48 **synthetic** couple profiles with labels citing facts and rules | `evaluation/benchmark/` | Dev yes; held-out labels sealed | - **Lawful access:** - HDB returns HTTP 403 to automated clients. That block was respected: pages were captured by hand, with no scraping or spoofing (D-055). - The HFE FAQ pages are excluded because robots.txt disallows them (D-060). - **Copyright:** - Snapshots are kept for computational analysis only (Copyright Act 2021 s 244). - Only authored paraphrases are tracked; no source text is. - HDB's Terms of Use ask for permission before linking or reuse. This prototype is private and locally run. Public deployment would need HDB's permission (D-057; residual risk, disclosed). - Facts carry `rights_review: overlap_checked`. The developer's final rights read (`cleared`) is pending. - **Privacy:** - Only fictional profiles are used, and the UI warns against entering real data. - User text is not logged. - Runtime calls send the fictional profile and the authored facts to Groq, never raw source text (D-054). - **Why synthetic profiles:** - Real applicant data would be personal data under the PDPA and isn't needed. - Hand-built profiles can target specific failure modes (missing fields, contradictions, exceptions, misconceptions, out-of-scope requests) that real logs would rarely contain in a small sample. - Each label cites the facts and rules it rests on. ## 6. Model selection **Selected:** `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on GroqCloud (D-067). One model is used for every configuration, at temperature 0, reasoning effort `low`, and strict `json_schema` output. - **Method:** a protocol registered before any output was produced (`evaluation/model_selection/protocol.md`). It used 12 dev cases, one prompt, one schema, the scorecard (accuracy 35, structured output 25, uncertainty 20, latency 10, cost 10) and minimum acceptance thresholds. - **Gemini 3.8 Flash** could not be evaluated: one-word probes took 25–104 s and one call returned HTTP 503. It was stopped for time, so **there was no head-to-head comparison**. - **gpt-oss-120b, direct generation:** - schema-valid 11/12 on the first attempt and 12/12 after one retry; - median latency 1.9 s; about US$0.0005 per call; - but policy accuracy 0.20, with critical errors in 7/12 cases. It **failed** the pre-registered accuracy and critical-error thresholds. This is disclosed rather than hidden. - Raw outputs and scores: `evaluation/model_selection/runs/20261028T201952Z/`. - **Operational justification:** - **Latency:** about 2 s per call suits a multi-call pipeline. - **Cost:** the lowest cost at scale of the candidates. - **Reproducibility and portability:** open weights (Apache-2.0) can be pinned, re-hosted or served locally. - **Data handling:** Groq keeps no inference data by default and offers zero data retention. - **Task fit:** the threshold failure shows the model's own HDB knowledge is unreliable. That is the case for grounding it in verified facts, not for trusting it directly. - **Rejected options:** - **Fine-tuning:** no rights-cleared training data, and policy changes over time. - **Local inference:** fictional data needs no on-premise processing, and laptop performance varies across reviewers. Revisit for real applicant data. ## 7. Evaluation **Design** (`docs/project_context/05_evaluation.md`, `evaluation/metric_spec.md`): an ablation of one pipeline. A (direct LLM) → B (+ retrieval) → C (+ profiling and rules) → D (+ verification), all with the same model, instructions, cases and output contract. - **Benchmark:** 48 synthetic cases in 6 categories × 8: standard, missing information, policy exception, misconception, conflicting details, out of scope. The split is group-aware (18 dev / 30 held-out), with near-duplicate families kept on one side. Held-out labels are Git-ignored and hash-committed, released only by a guarded loader (D-064). **No model or agent has seen them.** - **Primary metrics** (D-066, architecture-neutral; judged blind on the visible answer only): - critical-error rate (severity rubric: critical / major); - required-information coverage; - claim-level factual correctness and unsupported-claim rate; - missing-information recall and conflict identification; - appropriate abstention and over-abstention; - answer coverage and actionability. Factual correctness is scored separately from citation, so A is not penalised just for having no citation mechanism. - **Diagnostics** (never used to rank): structured-signal counts, citation traceability, retrieval recall@k, and the verifier (planned). - **Scorer:** the developer, blind. `evaluation.run sheet` exports answers under random IDs with the configuration hidden. **This scoring has not been done yet**, so no primary metric is reported below. - **Statistics planned:** exact McNemar and a paired bootstrap on paired cases, with failures kept in every denominator. - **Retrieval metric:** recall@3 suits single-answer retrieval. Here, dev cases carry 1–7 gold facts, so recall@3 is capped below 1 for many cases. The informative measure is recall at the k actually passed to generation (12), also reported normalised by min(k, number of gold facts). ## 8. Results (development set) > **Preliminary and diagnostic only.** 18 dev cases, one run per configuration, and no blind > primary scoring yet. These numbers describe **what the structured output contains**, not > whether it is correct. **No claim is made that B is better than A.** > Source: `evaluation/results/diagnostics_dev.json`. | Diagnostic (dev, n = 18) | A: direct | B: retrieval | |---|---|---| | Failed cases (kept in all counts) | 0 | 1 (DEV-12: HTTP 413, see below) | | Required missing fields listed in `missing_profile_fields` | 2/6 | 3/6 | | Expected conflicts flagged in `profile_conflicts` | 0/3 | 0/3 | | Out-of-scope requests flagged | 3/3 | 3/3 | | Whole answer refused on answerable cases | 0/9 | 0/9 | | Policy claims with an official source link | 0/34 | 33/35 | | Cited fact IDs that are among the case's gold facts | n/a | 19/50 | | Median latency per case (includes rate-limit waits) | 4.3 s | 15.7 s | | Total cost, 18 cases (list price) | US$0.0095 | US$0.0127 | **Retrieval (dev, 52 gold facts over 18 cases):** recall@3 0.23 · @5 0.33 · @8 0.42 · **@12 0.52**. This is well below the 0.90 target in D-031. Misses per case are listed in `diagnostics_dev.json`. **Observed behaviour** (developer review pending; observations, not scores): - **A states wrong policy confidently:** - HFE validity given as "one year" (DEV-10) or "6 months" (DEV-13), against 9 months in `HFE-VALID-001`; - "wait until he turns 21" instead of the under-21 core-occupier route (DEV-07); - an invented meaning of FT(PMC) (model selection, DEV-14). - **B gets the 9-month validity and the core-occupier route right, citing the facts.** It introduces a new error: it over-generalises the KB's "unconfirmed for engaged couples" note, which is about FT(PMC) priority, into "eligibility for engaged couples is unconfirmed" (DEV-07, DEV-10, DEV-13). - **Neither configuration flags contradictions** (0/3), and both sometimes assume missing values (DEV-05). That is exactly what C's deterministic profile checks are designed for. - **Out-of-scope requests** (grant amounts, ballot odds, singles) are declined by both. ## 9. Error analysis (dev, confirmed vs hypothesised) | Failure category | Cases | Observed | Expected | Likely cause | Remediation | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Pretrained-knowledge error (A) | DEV-07, 10, 13 | Wrong validity period; wrong under-21 route | 9 months; core occupier | No evidence (confirmed) | Retrieval (B fixes these cases) | | Retrieval miss | 13/18 cases miss ≥1 gold fact at k=12 | Generation lacks some facts | Gold facts present | Lexical gap between colloquial questions and fact text; multi-fact questions (confirmed by recall) | Rule-linked facts (C, by design); more aliases from dev misses only | | Evidence over-generalisation (B) | DEV-07, 10, 13 | "Engaged couples unconfirmed" | Unconfirmed only for FT(PMC) | Gap note retrieved out of context (hypothesis) | Retrieve gap notes only on matching topics (C's topic filter); verifier (D) | | Conflict not detected | DEV-13, 14, 15 | No conflict listed (A and B) | Neutral clarification | The LLM is not asked to compare statements systematically (hypothesis) | Deterministic conflict checks on the extracted profile (C) | | Rate-limit configuration | DEV-12 (B) | HTTP 413 "request too large" | An answer | `max_completion_tokens` 6000 + prompt exceeded the 8K tokens/min plan (confirmed) | Cap lowered to 4096 for future runs; saved run unchanged | ## 10. Limitations - **C and D are not built**, so the core hybrid hypothesis (rules + verification) is untested. The rule engine exists and is unit-tested but does not influence answers. - **No blind primary scoring and no held-out run.** Results are dev diagnostics from one run per configuration on 18 synthetic cases, with no statistical power. The benchmark is still a candidate (not frozen). - **Model:** failed its own pre-registered direct-generation thresholds. The alternative was unavailable during the session. - **Retrieval recall is low** (0.52 at k=12). - **Temporal fairness:** A relies on older pretrained knowledge, while B reads an October 2026 snapshot. B's advantage on facts partly reflects recency, not better reasoning. - **Policy currency:** facts reflect the 2026-10-28 snapshot. A live-page drift check (G-15) and the final rights clearance are pending. - **Structured output:** strict mode is not airtight on the provider (one invalid enum was observed and recovered by the retry). Latency includes waits for the free-plan rate limit. ## 11. Deployment considerations *(Described, not implemented.)* **Target users and environment:** first-time couples preparing for a BTO application, using a web assistant run by a public agency. It sits beside the official HDB Flat Portal, not inside it, and never collects NRIC or Singpass data. **Cost at scale:** configuration B used about 2,650 input and 520 output tokens per query, about US$0.0007 at gpt-oss-120b list prices. That is roughly US$70 a month for 100,000 queries. The full C/D design adds up to two calls, roughly tripling this to about US$0.002 per query. Retrieval and rules run on the CPU at negligible cost. **Monitoring:** weekly blind audits of sampled answers for critical-error rate; the share of policy claims with a valid citation; evidence-gap and out-of-scope rates by topic (a rise signals coverage holes); schema-failure and API-error rates; p95 latency and cost per query; and user "was this helpful" feedback. **Key risk: policy drift.** HDB changes a rule, for example the HFE validity period, while the knowledge base still holds the old fact, so the assistant confidently cites an official page that no longer says what it claims. Mitigation: monthly re-capture of source pages, with automated hash comparison flagging changed sections; facts from changed sections are suspended until re-verified; and every answer shows the "sources retrieved" date. ## 12. Development narrative - **Phase 0–1:** turned the brief and the approach document into a requirements register and a decision log (`docs/decisions.md`, D-001 onward). Scaffolded with uv, Docker and Streamlit. - **Phase 2:** - Automated capture (Playwright) was **dropped** after HDB returned 403. Bypassing the block would have undermined the "lawful access" defence, so capture became manual (D-055, D-056). - A PDF-parsing dependency was rejected in favour of manual review of 6 pages (D-052). - The HFE FAQs were dropped for robots.txt (D-060). - Facts were authored and verified against hash-pinned snapshots (D-058). The rules were kept as declarative YAML rather than code (D-038, D-062). - **Phase 3a:** benchmark and rubric written **before** any prompt work. Held-out labels were sealed with a hash commitment (D-063, D-064). Rule-ID recall was replaced by architecture-neutral content key points, so the A–D comparison stays fair (D-066). - **Phase 3b:** - **Model selection:** pre-registered; Gemini unavailable; Groq chosen despite failing its thresholds, with that disclosed (D-067). - **Baseline A:** built with fail-closed handling and 25 failure-mode tests. - **Time-boxing:** with about 1.5 h left, C and D were deferred in favour of B, a working Docker build and this documentation (D-069). Every failed attempt (an aborted harness run, Cloudflare and 413 errors) is recorded in `docs/development_log.md`. - **Tooling:** uv (reproducible lockfile); Pydantic (typed contracts); `openai` client (provider-agnostic); `rank-bm25` (deterministic, explainable retrieval); stdlib for evaluation. ## 13. AI coding agent usage - **Tool:** Claude Code (Anthropic), used throughout for requirements extraction, design drafting, code, tests and documentation. - **Developer's role:** every decision was approved by the developer and recorded with an ID in `docs/decisions.md`. The agent never committed or pushed. - **Constraints the agent worked under:** - It read private source snapshots only for fact authoring (D-054, with model training turned off for the account). - It never opened held-out labels (D-064). - It flagged rather than hid failures, such as the model's threshold failure. - **Session logs:** exported to `ai_logs/` *(to be added by the developer before submission; any redactions of private source text or identifying details will be listed in `ai_logs/REDACTIONS.md`)*.

applicants. You check each claim ONLY against the verified policy facts it cites. You do not

cat > src/bto_buddy/verification.py <<'EOF'
"""Claim-level verification (stage 7, D-034): deterministic checks first, then ONE batched
LLM judge for the remaining claims. Display policy (D-011):
  supported            -> show with its official source
  contradicted         -> withhold the claim and flag that something was withheld
  insufficient_evidence -> show only as "unconfirmed", without a source, plus an evidence gap
Claims are never rewritten and there is no regeneration. The original claims, the verdicts
and the judge's raw response are all kept.

Which claims are checked (D-065): every `policy_fact`, and any `preparation_step` that cites
a fact. Caveats and uncited procedural steps are not factual assertions about policy, so
they pass through unverified.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from pydantic import ValidationError

from bto_buddy.generation import PROMPT_DIR, strict_json_schema
from bto_buddy.llm import LLMClient, LLMError, estimate_cost_usd
from bto_buddy.schemas import (
    DisplayedClaim,
    EvidenceBundle,
    EvidenceGap,
    FinalGuidance,
    GeneratedClaim,
    JudgeOutput,
    UserRequest,
    VerificationResult,
)

VERIFY_PROMPT = "verify_v1"
_ACTION = {
    "supported": "show_with_source",
    "contradicted": "withhold_and_flag",
    "insufficient_evidence": "state_as_unconfirmed",
}


@dataclass
class VerifierRecord:
    """What the verifier did, for the prediction file (raw judge output kept)."""

    results: list[VerificationResult] = field(default_factory=list)
    judge_raw: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    judge_error: str | None = None
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    reasoning_tokens: int = 0
    latency_ms: int = 0
    llm_calls: int = 0


def checkable(c: GeneratedClaim) -> bool:
    return c.kind == "policy_fact" or (c.kind == "preparation_step" and bool(c.cited_fact_ids))


def _result(c: GeneratedClaim, outcome: str, method: str, why: str) -> VerificationResult:
    return VerificationResult(
        claim_id=c.claim_id,
        outcome=outcome,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        method=method,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        checked_fact_ids=list(c.cited_fact_ids),
        rationale=why,
        display_action=_ACTION[outcome],  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )


def deterministic_check(c: GeneratedClaim, bundle: EvidenceBundle) -> VerificationResult | None:
    """A hit decides the outcome without the LLM; None means 'send to the judge'."""
    if not c.cited_fact_ids:
        return _result(c, "insufficient_evidence", "deterministic", "No fact cited.")
    known = {e.fact_id for e in bundle.items}
    outside = [f for f in c.cited_fact_ids if f not in known]
    if outside:
        return _result(
            c, "insufficient_evidence", "deterministic", f"Cites facts not retrieved: {outside}"
        )
    return None


def judge_messages(
    request: UserRequest, claims: list[GeneratedClaim], bundle: EvidenceBundle
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    by_id = {e.fact_id: e for e in bundle.items}
    facts = sorted({f for c in claims for f in c.cited_fact_ids})
    fact_lines = []
    for f in facts:
        e = by_id[f]
        exc = f" Exceptions: {'; '.join(e.exceptions)}" if e.exceptions else ""
        fact_lines.append(f"[{f}] {e.statement}{exc}")
    claim_lines = [f"{c.claim_id} (cites {', '.join(c.cited_fact_ids)}): {c.text}" for c in claims]
    user = (
        f"<applicant_situation>\n{request.situation_text}\n</applicant_situation>\n\n"
        "<facts>\n" + "\n".join(fact_lines) + "\n</facts>\n\n"
        "<claims>\n" + "\n".join(claim_lines) + "\n</claims>"
    )
    system = (PROMPT_DIR / f"{VERIFY_PROMPT}.md").read_text()
    return [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]


def verify(
    request: UserRequest, claims: list[GeneratedClaim], bundle: EvidenceBundle, client: LLMClient
) -> VerifierRecord:
    rec = VerifierRecord()
    pending: list[GeneratedClaim] = []
    decided: dict[str, VerificationResult] = {}
    for c in claims:
        if not checkable(c):
            continue
        hit = deterministic_check(c, bundle)
        if hit is not None:
            decided[c.claim_id] = hit
        else:
            pending.append(c)
    if pending:
        rec.llm_calls = 1
        try:
            resp = client.complete(
                judge_messages(request, pending, bundle),
                "claim_verdicts",
                strict_json_schema(JudgeOutput),
            )
            rec.judge_raw = resp.raw
            rec.input_tokens, rec.output_tokens = resp.input_tokens, resp.output_tokens
            rec.reasoning_tokens, rec.latency_ms = resp.reasoning_tokens, resp.latency_ms
            verdicts = {v.claim_id: v for v in JudgeOutput.model_validate_json(resp.content).verdicts}
        except (LLMError, ValidationError) as e:
            # Fail closed: an unverifiable claim is shown only as unconfirmed.
            rec.judge_error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:500]}"
            if isinstance(e, LLMError):
                rec.judge_raw = e.raw
            verdicts = {}
        for c in pending:
            v = verdicts.get(c.claim_id)
            if v is None:
                why = "Judge returned no verdict." if rec.judge_error is None else rec.judge_error
                decided[c.claim_id] = _result(c, "insufficient_evidence", "llm_judge", why)
            else:
                decided[c.claim_id] = _result(c, v.outcome, "llm_judge", v.rationale)
    rec.results = [decided[c.claim_id] for c in claims if c.claim_id in decided]
    return rec


def apply_verification(
    pre: FinalGuidance, request: UserRequest, bundle: EvidenceBundle, client: LLMClient
) -> tuple[FinalGuidance, VerifierRecord]:
    """D = the given pre-verification guidance + verification. Takes B's output unchanged, so a
    B-vs-D comparison isolates verification (no new generation)."""
    if pre.run.status == "failed":
        rec = VerifierRecord()
        return pre.model_copy(update={"run": pre.run.model_copy(update={"config_id": "D"})}), rec
    claims = [d.claim for d in pre.claims]
    rec = verify(request, claims, bundle, client)
    by_claim = {r.claim_id: r for r in rec.results}
    displayed, gaps = [], [g for g in pre.evidence_gaps if g.kind != "claim_uncited"]
    for d in pre.claims:
        r = by_claim.get(d.claim.claim_id)
        sources = d.sources if r is None or r.outcome == "supported" else []
        displayed.append(DisplayedClaim(claim=d.claim, verification=r, sources=sources))
        if r is not None and r.outcome != "supported":
            withheld = r.outcome == "contradicted"
            gaps.append(
                EvidenceGap(
                    topic=None,
                    claim_id=d.claim.claim_id,
                    kind="claim_unsupported" if withheld else "claim_uncited"
                    if not d.claim.cited_fact_ids
                    else "claim_unsupported",
                    detail=(
                        "A statement was withheld because our sources contradict it."
                        if withheld
                        else f"Not confirmed by our sources: {d.claim.text}"
                    ),
                    official_source_url="https://www.hdb.gov.sg",
                )
            )
    run = pre.run
    tokens_in, tokens_out = run.input_tokens + rec.input_tokens, run.output_tokens + rec.output_tokens
    new_run = run.model_copy(
        update={
            "config_id": "D",
            "prompt_versions": {**run.prompt_versions, "verify": VERIFY_PROMPT},
            "llm_calls": run.llm_calls + rec.llm_calls,
            "input_tokens": tokens_in,
            "output_tokens": tokens_out,
            "reasoning_tokens": run.reasoning_tokens + rec.reasoning_tokens,
            "latency_ms": run.latency_ms + rec.latency_ms,
            "estimated_cost_usd": estimate_cost_usd(run.model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out),
            "error": f"verifier: {rec.judge_error}" if rec.judge_error else run.error,
        }
    )
    return pre.model_copy(
        update={"claims": displayed, "evidence_gaps": gaps, "run": new_run}
    ), rec


def record_json(rec: VerifierRecord) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return json.loads(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "results": [r.model_dump(mode="json") for r in rec.results],
                "judge_raw": rec.judge_raw,
                "judge_error": rec.judge_error,
                "input_tokens": rec.input_tokens,
                "output_tokens": rec.output_tokens,
                "latency_ms": rec.latency_ms,
                "llm_calls": rec.llm_calls,
            }
        )
    )
EOF

"""Claim-level verification (stage 7, D-034): deterministic checks first, then ONE batched
LLM judge for the remaining claims. Display policy (D-011):
  supported            -> show with its official source
  contradicted         -> withhold the claim and flag that something was withheld
  insufficient_evidence -> show only as "unconfirmed", without a source, plus an evidence gap
Claims are never rewritten and there is no regeneration. The original claims, the verdicts
and the judge's raw response are all kept.

Which claims are checked (D-065): every `policy_fact`, and any `preparation_step` that cites
a fact. Caveats and uncited procedural steps are not factual assertions about policy, so
they pass through unverified.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from pydantic import ValidationError

from bto_buddy.generation import PROMPT_DIR, strict_json_schema
from bto_buddy.llm import LLMClient, LLMError, estimate_cost_usd
from bto_buddy.schemas import (
    DisplayedClaim,
    EvidenceBundle,
    EvidenceGap,
    FinalGuidance,
    GeneratedClaim,
    JudgeOutput,
    UserRequest,
    VerificationResult,
)

VERIFY_PROMPT = "verify_v1"
_ACTION = {
    "supported": "show_with_source",
    "contradicted": "withhold_and_flag",
    "insufficient_evidence": "state_as_unconfirmed",
}


@dataclass
class VerifierRecord:
    """What the verifier did, for the prediction file (raw judge output kept)."""

    results: list[VerificationResult] = field(default_factory=list)
    judge_raw: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    judge_error: str | None = None
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    reasoning_tokens: int = 0
    latency_ms: int = 0
    llm_calls: int = 0


def checkable(c: GeneratedClaim) -> bool:
    return c.kind == "policy_fact" or (c.kind == "preparation_step" and bool(c.cited_fact_ids))


def _result(c: GeneratedClaim, outcome: str, method: str, why: str) -> VerificationResult:
    return VerificationResult(
        claim_id=c.claim_id,
        outcome=outcome,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        method=method,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        checked_fact_ids=list(c.cited_fact_ids),
        rationale=why,
        display_action=_ACTION[outcome],  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )


def deterministic_check(c: GeneratedClaim, bundle: EvidenceBundle) -> VerificationResult | None:
    """A hit decides the outcome without the LLM; None means 'send to the judge'."""
    if not c.cited_fact_ids:
        return _result(c, "insufficient_evidence", "deterministic", "No fact cited.")
    known = {e.fact_id for e in bundle.items}
    outside = [f for f in c.cited_fact_ids if f not in known]
    if outside:
        return _result(
            c, "insufficient_evidence", "deterministic", f"Cites facts not retrieved: {outside}"
        )
    return None


def judge_messages(
    request: UserRequest, claims: list[GeneratedClaim], bundle: EvidenceBundle
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    by_id = {e.fact_id: e for e in bundle.items}
    facts = sorted({f for c in claims for f in c.cited_fact_ids})
    fact_lines = []
    for f in facts:
        e = by_id[f]
        exc = f" Exceptions: {'; '.join(e.exceptions)}" if e.exceptions else ""
        fact_lines.append(f"[{f}] {e.statement}{exc}")
    claim_lines = [f"{c.claim_id} (cites {', '.join(c.cited_fact_ids)}): {c.text}" for c in claims]
    user = (
        f"<applicant_situation>\n{request.situation_text}\n</applicant_situation>\n\n"
        "<facts>\n" + "\n".join(fact_lines) + "\n</facts>\n\n"
        "<claims>\n" + "\n".join(claim_lines) + "\n</claims>"
    )
    system = (PROMPT_DIR / f"{VERIFY_PROMPT}.md").read_text()
    return [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]


def verify(
    request: UserRequest, claims: list[GeneratedClaim], bundle: EvidenceBundle, client: LLMClient
) -> VerifierRecord:
    rec = VerifierRecord()
    pending: list[GeneratedClaim] = []
    decided: dict[str, VerificationResult] = {}
    for c in claims:
        if not checkable(c):
            continue
        hit = deterministic_check(c, bundle)
        if hit is not None:
            decided[c.claim_id] = hit
        else:
            pending.append(c)
    if pending:
        rec.llm_calls = 1
        try:
            resp = client.complete(
                judge_messages(request, pending, bundle),
                "claim_verdicts",
                strict_json_schema(JudgeOutput),
            )
            rec.judge_raw = resp.raw
            rec.input_tokens, rec.output_tokens = resp.input_tokens, resp.output_tokens
            rec.reasoning_tokens, rec.latency_ms = resp.reasoning_tokens, resp.latency_ms
            verdicts = {v.claim_id: v for v in JudgeOutput.model_validate_json(resp.content).verdicts}
        except (LLMError, ValidationError) as e:
            # Fail closed: an unverifiable claim is shown only as unconfirmed.
            rec.judge_error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:500]}"
            if isinstance(e, LLMError):
                rec.judge_raw = e.raw
            verdicts = {}
        for c in pending:
            v = verdicts.get(c.claim_id)
            if v is None:
                why = "Judge returned no verdict." if rec.judge_error is None else rec.judge_error
                decided[c.claim_id] = _result(c, "insufficient_evidence", "llm_judge", why)
            else:
                decided[c.claim_id] = _result(c, v.outcome, "llm_judge", v.rationale)
    rec.results = [decided[c.claim_id] for c in claims if c.claim_id in decided]
    return rec


def apply_verification(
    pre: FinalGuidance, request: UserRequest, bundle: EvidenceBundle, client: LLMClient
) -> tuple[FinalGuidance, VerifierRecord]:
    """D = the given pre-verification guidance + verification. Takes B's output unchanged, so a
    B-vs-D comparison isolates verification (no new generation)."""
    if pre.run.status == "failed":
        rec = VerifierRecord()
        return pre.model_copy(update={"run": pre.run.model_copy(update={"config_id": "D"})}), rec
    claims = [d.claim for d in pre.claims]
    rec = verify(request, claims, bundle, client)
    by_claim = {r.claim_id: r for r in rec.results}
    displayed, gaps = [], [g for g in pre.evidence_gaps if g.kind != "claim_uncited"]
    for d in pre.claims:
        r = by_claim.get(d.claim.claim_id)
        sources = d.sources if r is None or r.outcome == "supported" else []
        displayed.append(DisplayedClaim(claim=d.claim, verification=r, sources=sources))
        if r is not None and r.outcome != "supported":
            withheld = r.outcome == "contradicted"
            gaps.append(
                EvidenceGap(
                    topic=None,
                    claim_id=d.claim.claim_id,
                    kind="claim_unsupported" if withheld else "claim_uncited"
                    if not d.claim.cited_fact_ids
                    else "claim_unsupported",
                    detail=(
                        "A statement was withheld because our sources contradict it."
                        if withheld
                        else f"Not confirmed by our sources: {d.claim.text}"
                    ),
                    official_source_url="https://www.hdb.gov.sg",
                )
            )
    run = pre.run
    tokens_in, tokens_out = run.input_tokens + rec.input_tokens, run.output_tokens + rec.output_tokens
    new_run = run.model_copy(
        update={
            "config_id": "D",
            "prompt_versions": {**run.prompt_versions, "verify": VERIFY_PROMPT},
            "llm_calls": run.llm_calls + rec.llm_calls,
            "input_tokens": tokens_in,
            "output_tokens": tokens_out,
            "reasoning_tokens": run.reasoning_tokens + rec.reasoning_tokens,
            "latency_ms": run.latency_ms + rec.latency_ms,
            "estimated_cost_usd": estimate_cost_usd(run.model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out),
            "error": f"verifier: {rec.judge_error}" if rec.judge_error else run.error,
        }
    )
    return pre.model_copy(
        update={"claims": displayed, "evidence_gaps": gaps, "run": new_run}
    ), rec


def record_json(rec: VerifierRecord) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return json.loads(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "results": [r.model_dump(mode="json") for r in rec.results],
                "judge_raw": rec.judge_raw,
                "judge_error": rec.judge_error,
                "input_tokens": rec.input_tokens,
                "output_tokens": rec.output_tokens,
                "latency_ms": rec.latency_ms,
                "llm_calls": rec.llm_calls,
            }
        )
    )

   HH-SUBSIDY-001: A person has taken a housing subsidy if they previously bought a flat from HDB, bought a resale flat with a CPF housing grant, bought a DBSS flat or an EC unit from a developer, or benefited from another housing subsidy such as SERS or HUDC privatisation. A core member who has taken a subsidy is a second-timer; buyers who have not are first-timers. EXC: A couple made up of one first-timer and one second-timer is still treated as a first-timer family for priority purposes.

HDB's Employment Status Guide sets out six: Unemployed, Full-time National Serviceman, Full-time student, Employed with CPF contributions, Employed without CPF contributions, and Self-Employed. The examples it gives are not exhaustive.

cd "<repo>" && cat > tests/test_verification.py <<'EOF'
"""Configuration D plumbing (no network). The judge's semantic accuracy (negation, numbers,
exceptions, applicability) needs a real model and is evaluated on dev claims instead
(evaluation/results/*-D-dev/verifier_eval.json); here canned verdicts test that every
outcome is handled and displayed as D-011 requires."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import date
from typing import Any

from bto_buddy import pipeline, verification
from bto_buddy.llm import LLMError
from bto_buddy.schemas import UserRequest
from test_baseline import VALID, FakeClient

REQ = UserRequest(
    request_id="T-D",
    situation_text="We are an engaged Singapore Citizen couple, both first-timers.",
    question="How long is the HFE letter valid?",
    as_of=date(2026, 11, 1),
)
BUNDLE = pipeline.retrieve_for(REQ)
F1, F2 = BUNDLE.items[0].fact_id, BUNDLE.items[1].fact_id


def claim(cid: str, kind: str, cited: list[str], text: str = "x") -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"claim_id": cid, "text": text, "kind": kind, "cited_fact_ids": cited}


GEN = {
    **VALID,
    "claims": [
        claim("c1", "policy_fact", [F1], "Valid for 9 months."),
        claim("c2", "policy_fact", [F2], "Valid for 12 months."),  # judge: contradicted
        claim("c3", "policy_fact", [F1], "Also covers resale."),  # judge: insufficient
        claim("c4", "policy_fact", [], "Uncited rule."),  # deterministic: insufficient
        claim("c5", "caveat", [], "Check hdb.gov.sg."),  # not checked
        claim("c6", "preparation_step", [], "Gather documents."),  # uncited step: not checked
    ],
}


def verdicts(**outcomes: str) -> str:
    return json.dumps(
        {"verdicts": [{"claim_id": c, "outcome": o, "rationale": "r"} for c, o in outcomes.items()]}
    )


def run_d(*judge: str | LLMError) -> Any:
    client = FakeClient(json.dumps(GEN), *judge)
    return pipeline.run_verified(REQ, client), client


def test_outcomes_map_to_display_actions_and_render() -> None:
    g, client = run_d(verdicts(c1="supported", c2="contradicted", c3="insufficient_evidence"))
    by = {d.claim.claim_id: d for d in g.claims}
    assert by["c1"].verification.display_action == "show_with_source" and by["c1"].sources
    assert by["c2"].verification.display_action == "withhold_and_flag" and not by["c2"].sources
    assert by["c3"].verification.display_action == "state_as_unconfirmed" and not by["c3"].sources
    assert by["c4"].verification.method == "deterministic"
    assert by["c5"].verification is None and by["c6"].verification is None
    text = pipeline.render_answer(g)
    assert "Valid for 12 months." not in text  # withheld claim never shown (REQ-VER-007)
    assert "withheld" in text and "Also covers resale. (Unconfirmed" in text
    assert g.run.config_id == "D" and g.run.llm_calls == 2
    assert g.run.prompt_versions["verify"] == verification.VERIFY_PROMPT
    # Only judge-bound claims (cited, in bundle) are sent to the judge.
    judge_user = client.calls[1][1]["content"]
    assert "c1 (cites" in judge_user and "c4" not in judge_user and "c5" not in judge_user


def test_original_claims_are_never_rewritten() -> None:
    g, _ = run_d(verdicts(c1="supported", c2="contradicted", c3="insufficient_evidence"))
    assert [d.claim.text for d in g.claims] == [c["text"] for c in GEN["claims"]]


def test_judge_failure_fails_closed_to_unconfirmed() -> None:
    g, _ = run_d(LLMError("timeout", "slow"))
    checked = [d for d in g.claims if d.verification is not None]
    assert all(d.verification.outcome == "insufficient_evidence" for d in checked)
    assert all(not d.sources for d in checked)
    assert g.run.error and g.run.error.startswith("verifier:")


def test_missing_verdict_is_insufficient() -> None:

from datetime import date
from typing import Any

    as_of=date(2026, 11, 1),
)

F1, F2 = BUNDLE.items[0].fact_id, BUNDLE.items[1].fact_id


def claim(cid: str, kind: str, cited: list[str], text: str = "x") -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"claim_id": cid, "text": text, "kind": kind, "cited_fact_ids": cited}


GEN = {
    **VALID,
    "claims": [
        claim("c1", "policy_fact", [F1], "Valid for 9 months."),
        claim("c2", "policy_fact", [F2], "Valid for 12 months."),  # judge: contradicted
        claim("c3", "policy_fact", [F1], "Also covers resale."),  # judge: insufficient
        claim("c4", "policy_fact", [], "Uncited rule."),  # deterministic: insufficient
        claim("c5", "caveat", [], "Check hdb.gov.sg."),  # not checked
        claim("c6", "preparation_step", [], "Gather documents."),  # uncited step: not checked
    ],
}


def verdicts(**outcomes: str) -> str:
    return json.dumps(
        {"verdicts": [{"claim_id": c, "outcome": o, "rationale": "r"} for c, o in outcomes.items()]}

    assert by["c2"].verification.display_action == "withhold_and_flag" and not by["c2"].sources
    assert by["c3"].verification.display_action == "state_as_unconfirmed" and not by["c3"].sources
    assert by["c4"].verification.method == "deterministic"

content.text:
I built D (claim verification) rather than C, and the project now has its hybrid comparison: **B vs D**. D re-checks B's *saved* answers, so the generated text is identical and only verification differs. The architecture defines D as C plus the verifier; building it on B instead is a deviation, recorded as D-071 and stated in the README.

**How D works:** claims with no citation, or citing a fact that wasn't retrieved, are marked insufficient without calling the model. Everything else goes to one batched judge call (same model) that sees only the cited facts and the applicant's situation. Supported claims show with their source; contradicted claims are withheld and flagged; insufficient ones show as "unconfirmed" with no source. Claims are never rewritten, and if the judge fails, claims fall back to "unconfirmed". The app has a D mode, and a live D answer inside the rebuilt Docker container worked: the 9-month claim was verified, in 2.2 s.

## Findings (dev, 49 checked claims)
I labelled these myself after the run, so they're indicative, not developer-blind; the README says so.

| My label \ verifier said | supported | contradicted | insufficient |
|---|---|---|---|
| supported (27) | 27 | 0 | 0 |
| contradicted (8) | **4** | 1 | 3 |
| insufficient (14) | **2** | 0 | 12 |

import random

from typing import Any

from evaluation.run import RESULTS, load_predictions

SEED = 20261029
N_BOOT = 10_000

    "standard",
    "missing_information",
    "policy_exception",
    "misconception",
    "conflicting",
    "out_of_scope",

def mcnemar_exact(b: int, c: int) -> float:
    """Two-sided exact McNemar p-value from the discordant counts b and c (binomial, p=0.5)."""

        "missing_information_recall": ratio(
            sum(o["missing_hits"] for o in outs), sum(o["missing_den"] for o in outs)

        "pending_human_metrics": [
            "critical-error rate (labelled + unlabelled critical errors)",
            "required-information coverage (content key points)",
            "claim-level factual correctness for A",
            "actionability",
        ],
        "not_applicable": {
            "required_rule_recall": "C is not built; no configuration applies rules "

        },
        "overall": {},
        "by_category": defaultdict(dict),

        out: dict[str, Any] = {}

        xs = [per_cfg[x_cfg][case_ids[i]] for i in sel]
        ys = [per_cfg[y_cfg][case_ids[i]] for i in sel]

        yb = [int(o["missing_hits"] == o["missing_den"]) for o in ys]
        b = sum(1 for p, q in zip(xb, yb, strict=True) if p and not q)
        c = sum(1 for p, q in zip(xb, yb, strict=True) if q and not p)
        out["all_missing_fields_listed"] = {
            "cases": len(sel), f"{x_cfg}_only": b, f"{y_cfg}_only": c,
            "mcnemar_exact_p": round(mcnemar_exact(b, c), 4),

        yb = [int(per_cfg[y_cfg][case_ids[i]]["covered"]) for i in sel]
        b = sum(1 for p, q in zip(xb, yb, strict=True) if p and not q)
        c = sum(1 for p, q in zip(xb, yb, strict=True) if q and not p)
        out["answer_covered"] = {
            "cases": len(sel), f"{x_cfg}_only": b, f"{y_cfg}_only": c,
            "mcnemar_exact_p": round(mcnemar_exact(b, c), 4),
        }
        # Per-case missing-information recall, paired bootstrap.
        sel = [i for i, lb in enumerate(labs) if lb.required_missing_fields]
        out["missing_information_recall_bootstrap"] = paired_bootstrap(
            [per_cfg[x_cfg][case_ids[i]]["missing_hits"] / labs[i].__len__() if False else
             per_cfg[x_cfg][case_ids[i]]["missing_hits"] / per_cfg[x_cfg][case_ids[i]]["missing_den"]
             for i in sel],
            [per_cfg[y_cfg][case_ids[i]]["missing_hits"] / per_cfg[y_cfg][case_ids[i]]["missing_den"]
             for i in sel],
        )
        return out

    cfgs = list(runs)
    for x_cfg, y_cfg in zip(cfgs, cfgs[1:], strict=False):

    if "D" in runs:

    report["by_category"] = dict(report["by_category"])
    return report

    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if len(args) != 3:
        raise SystemExit(__doc__)
    report = evaluate(dict(zip(["A", "B", "D"], args, strict=True)))
    out = RESULTS / "metrics_dev.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=1))
    print(json.dumps({k: report[k] for k in ("overall", "paired", "claim_level_B_vs_D")}, indent=1))
    print(f"wrote {out.relative_to(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])}")

    main()
